clue.text: Jacob is not thinking clearly

definitions.meaning: a Jacob is a breed of sheep with a thick fleece covering its head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacob' looks like a man's name, but here it is the spotted, horned sheep breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jacob sheep literally has a fleecy head, and the idiom describes someone muddled and vague in thought.

clue.text: Reportedly makes a mess of meat dish in Welsh place

indicators.note: reportedly means we are told how the phrase is heard when spoken

parts.words: makes a mess of meat dish
parts.note: to make a mess of is to wreck, and a meat dish here is ham

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a plate of meat in a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: WRECKS HAM, said out loud, sounds like the name of WREXHAM, a town in north-east Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrexham is a town in north Wales, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Remain longer, camping?

definitions.meaning: to stay beyond the expected time
camping is a stay out of doors

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as OUT + STAY: camping is staying outdoors, and the question mark flags the wordplay sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstay is to remain past the time allowed, and a camping trip is a stay spent outdoors.

clue.text: Northerner having a scheme adopted by Lord with little hesitation

indicators.note: something adopted by another is taken into it, so the scheme goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: a scheme is a plan, with the article A kept
er is the small sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A northern person has a plan which a peer takes up with a slight pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' signals the container: the plan is taken into the abbreviated peer, and 'with' tacks on the hesitation sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapland lies in the far north of Scandinavia, so a native of it is a northern person.

clue.text: Some behave suspiciously they're the owners

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people act shiftily, and those are the property holders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks out a run of letters from 'beHAVE Suspiciously'. The haves and have-nots are the rich and the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: The haves are the wealthy, the people who possess property, as opposed to the have-nots.

clue.text: A job given to the French missionary

parts.note: a post is a job or position
le is the French masculine form of the

explanation.surface: A French person is given a posting as a missionary.
explanation.walkthrough: LE is French for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the first Christian messengers sent out to preach, so one is a missionary.

clue.text: Teams are level-even — sometimes, in some places

indicators.note: the answer sits within some of the letters of the phrase, spanning its words

explanation.surface: A remark that sports sides are evenly matched only now and then, in certain areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in some places' points to the run hidden in 'levEL-EVEN Sometimes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket and football sides have eleven players, so the teams are called elevens.

clue.text: Marcatissimo playing which Shostakovich had a problem with?

definitions.text: which Shostakovich had a problem with?

indicators.note: playing suggests the musical term is performed in a different way, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavily accented passage of music that troubled a Soviet composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcatissimo, 'very strongly accented', is a music term that anagrams to the answer. Shostakovich was censured by Soviet officials, and in the USSR the ministries were called commissariats.
explanation.definitionFit: Shostakovich was denounced by the Soviet authorities, the state commissariat for culture among them.

clue.text: Become more exalted from plain work

parts.note: something plain is open to view, overt
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone rises in rank thanks to honest labour.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise higher than or surpass something, so to become loftier.

clue.text: Flower carries name showing it is wild

indicators.note: a flower that carries something holds it within itself

parts.note: the violet is a small purple flower

explanation.surface: A bloom with a label proves it is an uncultivated plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' puts N inside VIOLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent and wild both describe behaviour that is uncontrolled and fierce.

clue.text: Incline to retain right arrangement as formative

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so the letter is held inside

parts.note: to incline to is to tend
a setting is an arrangement, as of music or jewels

explanation.surface: A tendency to keep the correct layout is described as shaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain' puts R inside TEND, making TREND.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendsetting influences and shapes what follows, so it is formative of fashion.

clue.text: It indicates respected headgear

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'It indicates respected headgear', supplies only HAT for the HAT in MA(HAT)MA; the MA ... MA wordplay is missing, so the newspaper OCR has likely cut or garbled the clue and no scan or reprint gives the rest.

clue.text: That'll teach you there's a drunk in this place

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
here means in this place

explanation.surface: A taunt pointing out a drunk standing right here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's' is a link word joining the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are triumphant retorts said to someone shown to be in the wrong.

clue.text: Monotonous writer coming in to speak

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to say is to speak
the writer of the clue refers to the setter as me

explanation.surface: A dull author arrives to give a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'writer'; 'coming in' signals that the writer goes inside the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Samey means tediously unvaried, lacking variety, which is what monotonous means.

clue.text: Low estate, maybe, featured in legal document

indicators.note: something featured in another appears inside it

parts.note: a deed is a legal document, as for a property
the press is called the fourth estate, so it is one example of an estate

explanation.surface: A humble property appears in the papers of a legal transaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estate' looks like land, but the press is called the 'fourth estate'; 'featured in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low and feeling depressed are both ways of being in poor spirits.

clue.text: Steal sign of gold alloy

parts.note: to pinch is to steal
a beck is a beckoning gesture, as in beck and call

explanation.surface: Thieving a symbol made of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: A beck is a summoning nod or gesture, as in 'at someone's beck and call'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinchbeck is a copper and zinc alloy made to imitate gold, used in cheap jewellery.

clue.text: Star upset blade on Irish islands

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland

explanation.surface: A knife is knocked over on islands off Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges BLADE to ALDEB.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is the bright red giant in the constellation Taurus, a well-known star.

clue.text: Cover put over girl cause a problem

indicators.note: in a down clue, put over means turned upside down, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Putting a blanket on a girl creates difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put over' turns LID to DIL; 'cause' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between options, a predicament or quandary.

clue.text: Block and stop anger

parts.note: to bar is to stop or prevent
rage is intense anger

explanation.surface: Instructions to obstruct and halt fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word joining the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a dam or barrier built across a river, so it blocks the flow.

clue.text: Leek building incorporates British college

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body, so one piece goes inside
building suggests construction from parts, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A building made of vegetables includes something British in a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges LEEK to KELE; 'incorporates' puts B inside it. Keble is a college of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Keble is one of the colleges that make up Oxford University.

clue.text: King at university has to stay with one Middle Easterner

parts.note: K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king
U stands for university
to wait is to stay put
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A monarch at college must remain with a person from the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Kuwait is a Gulf state, so its people are from the Middle East.

clue.text: Where you could find the sweet results of industry

definitions.text: Where you could find the sweet results of industry

parts.words: Where you could find the sweet results of industry
parts.note: the sweet results are honey, made by hard-working bees, and the place to find it is their home

explanation.walkthrough: 'Industry' suggests factories, but it is the busy work of bees and its sweet result is honey.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees make and store honey in their hives, so a hive is where the honey is kept.

clue.text: Embarrassed after incorrect bill is brought up rudely

indicators.note: after means the colour word comes after the rearranged letters
incorrect means wrong, so the letters of the word are put in the wrong order

parts.note: embarrassed people go red in the face

explanation.surface: Someone blushes after a wrong invoice arrives, a sign of poor manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrect' is the anagram signal on 'bill', and 'after' puts the blushing colour behind it; 'brought up' means raised, not mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill-bred was raised badly and so shows bad manners.

clue.text: After romancing wed lieutenant and made a home

indicators.note: romancing means telling fanciful stories, so the letters of the word are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: Following a courtship, a soldier marries and settles down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After romancing' reads as a time phrase but is the anagram signal on 'wed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live in a place, so dwelt means lived or settled there.

clue.text: However archaic a greeting, live with it

parts.note: how is a traditional greeting, as in how do you do
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned hello, and a decision to live with it anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'archaic' says the definition is an old word for however.
explanation.definitionFit: Howbeit is an old-fashioned word for nevertheless or although.

clue.text: Mould found by business graduate in roof covering

indicators.note: in means the graduate is placed inside the roof covering

parts.note: a tile is a piece of roof covering
MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A fungus is discovered by a management graduate in the roofing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mould' looks like fungus, but it is a cooking mould; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbale is a drum-shaped mould for cooking, and the dish made in it.

clue.text: Treason abandoned by second printing of newspaper

indicators.note: abandoned by means the letter for second is left out

parts.note: sedition is incitement against the state, close to treason

explanation.surface: A traitor is deserted by an assistant in a newspaper story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' removes S from SEDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one print run or version of a newspaper.

clue.text: I take felt pen having design which can be used to make a picture

definitions.text: which can be used to make a picture

indicators.note: having a design means the letters are given a new pattern or arrangement

explanation.surface: An artist picks up a felt-tip pen with a plan for creating a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having design' rearranges I TAKE FELT PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter mixes and applies oil paint with this flexible blade.
